To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human language is an integrated system that arose from the linking of a preadapted expression system and a lexical system.

(1) the integration hypothesis is a viable explanation for the emergence of human syntax in evolution, and (2) the emergence of human syntactic Merge was a sudden event, and did not involve a series of gradual stages.
the emergence of language was rapid, and was achieved by the integration of two preadapted systems, one an expression system and the other a lexical system.

a radical rethinking of the evolution of language and its structure, and the role that syntax plays in this.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

language is the result of the integration of two pre adapted biological systems, which are found in the animal world and which have been integrated by the combinatorial operation, Merge, which is unique to language.
the emergence of language was not a gradual process, but a rapid one.
the rapid emergence of language in evolution was triggered by the integration of two pre adapted expression and lexical systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of two pre adapted modules, expression and lexical, gave rise to a full fledged human language in a very short time.
the emergence of language was a rapid process, and the first step was the integration of these preadapted systems.
language arose from a rapid integration of two pre existing systems in the human mind and not as a gradual evolution from a protolinguistic state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rapidity of emergence of language is due to the fact that the combinatorial operation, Merge was pre adapted to combine words and phrases, and this is what gave rise to the rapid emergence of language.
the integration hypothesis is a more parsimonious explanation for the rapid emergence of language than the gradualist view.
the emergence and development of human language is a rapid process, which took place in a short period of time, perhaps as little as a few tens of thousands of years.
